title: Eviction mitigation playbook: resize reservations and adaptive burst tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a high-traffic window on 2026-03-10 we observed a cluster-wide eviction spike in our dedicated clusters serving Redwood Dedicated customers. Multiple customer routes experienced degraded throughput and increased tail latency as GPUs entered eviction cycles when reservations were exhausted and burst policy allowed aggressive transient allocations.

This ticket consolidates the incident follow-up and defines a concrete playbook for: (1) corrective reservation resizing, (2) adaptive burst policy tuning to avoid unhealthy preemption, and (3) noisy-neighbor isolation techniques for long-running heavy workloads. The goal is to reduce eviction frequency by >= 90% for similarly shaped workloads and to provide runbook steps so on-call can quickly mitigate future events.

Incident timeline (short):
- 2026-03-10 02:17 UTC: First eviction alerts from telemetry (eviction-rate > 5% across cluster A).
- 2026-03-10 02:22 UTC: Routing fallback triggered for affected customers; elevated 5xx and increased per-token cost reported.
- 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC: On-call throttled burst policy and increased reservation sizes for two affected pools as an emergency mitigation.
- 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC: Eviction rate dropped below baseline; services partially recovered.

Root causes (synthesized):
1) Reservation mis-sizing: historical reservation sizing was based on average throughput; sudden traffic skew with long context generations increased concurrent KV cache/resident memory pressure beyond reserved working set.
2) Liberal burst policy: current burst controller permits transient allocations up to 3x reservation for short intervals without factoring in eviction risk heuristics, causing preemption of lower-priority resident workloads.
3) Noisy neighbors: several long-running interactive sessions (fine-tuning and beam-like decoding) held large KV caches and pinned memory. Isolation was insufficient because QoS and kernel-level cgroups did not separate cache-heavy vs compute-heavy consumers.

Action items (owner, priority, deliverable, status):
- A. Reservation sizing audit (Evan Chen, P0): run a week-long telemetry analysis to propose adjusted baseline reservation per-pool (deliverable: reservations_proposal.md). Status: In progress.
- B. Implement soft-eviction thresholds (Marco Ruiz, P0): add an intermediate threshold to graceful-shed low-priority bursts before kernel eviction. Deliverable: PR #8347. Status: In Review.
- C. Adaptive burst controller (SRE team / Priya Nair, P0): change policy to a dynamic burst budget that considers current eviction window and KV hit-rate. Deliverable: design doc + rollout plan. Status: Planned.
- D. Noisy-neighbor classification (Research/Applied ML - Lena Gomez, P1): build heuristic to tag sessions with high resident memory growth and recommend isolation. Deliverable: classifier model and explainability dashboard. Status: Backlog.
- E. Runbook updates & incident playbook (Aisha Patel, P0): publish step-by-step mitigation steps for on-call. Deliverable: confluence/playbooks/dedicated-eviction-mitigation. Status: Done (draft).

Decisions & trade-offs made so far:
- Temporary reservation bump versus long-term cost: for emergency mitigation we increased reservations for two pools by 20% to stop evictions. Trade-off: increased short-term unit cost but prevented sustained customer disruption. Long-term plan is to tune burst policy and classifier to avoid permanent reservation increases.
- Soft-eviction vs immediate preemption: we prefer a staged shedding (reduce burst budgets, GC KV caches, then preempt) to avoid losing warm KV caches that would harm latency. This adds implementation complexity but preserves QoE.

Telemetry and dashboards referenced:
- Grafana: /d/redwood/dedicated-eviction-weekly?orgId=1 (eviction-rate, tail-p99 latency, reservation-utilization)
- BigQuery query: projects/redwood-prod/queries/eviction_analysis_2026_03_10.sql
- Incident timeline doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IN/2026-03-10+Dedicated+Eviction+Spike

Acceptance criteria (how we will judge success):
- Primary: Eviction-rate for affected clusters reduced by >= 90% for comparable load shape across two subsequent synthetic load tests.
- Secondary: No customer-facing 5xx incidents related to eviction in a 14-day rolling window after rollout.
- Operational: On-call runbook reduces mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for eviction events by >= 50% versus this incident.

Rollout plan (high-level):
1) Short term (hotfix): merge PR #8347 (soft-eviction thresholds), release to canary clusters within 48h.
2) Mid term (2 weeks): telemetry-driven reservation resizing implemented via reservations_proposal.md and automated reservations API.
3) Longer term (6 weeks): deploy adaptive burst controller with chaos test and A/B rollout using canary tags.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Overly aggressive reservation reduction after changes could starve workloads. Mitigation: conservative 10% initial change and monitor.
- Risk: Adaptive burst controller complexity introduces regressions. Mitigation: strong unit/integration tests, staged rollout, rollback plan.

Current status & next steps:
- PR #8347 submitted and under review; contains the soft-shedding controller and integration tests.
- Telemetry analysis in progress (Evan) with draft reservations_proposal.md expected 2026-03-18.
- Update runbook with exact Grafana links and CLI commands for emergency operators (Aisha).

If you are assigned one of the action items, add a short comment below with ETA and blockers. For reviewers: please validate the soft-eviction acceptance tests in CI and sign off on PR #8347.
